samples.identification: Herramienta Para Respaldar Correo By Alexx v2.1 (12/07/2022), C++ batch wrapper
evidence: The CRT reaches the real application main at VA 0x401530. getenv(APPDATA) builds staging paths; calls through 0x41a9c0 resolve to msvcrt.system.

Two Base64 bodies in .rdata decode to a directory-creation script and the complete visible Outlook-backup batch. The wrapper writes them, invokes certutil -decode, calls the resulting batch, and applies hidden/system attributes.

The backup script logs locally, force-closes Outlook to release mail stores, copies current-directory *.pst and *.ost with xcopy /i /d /y into C:\RESPALDO CORREO, then starts Outlook. No credential extraction, destructive mail operation, remote upload, or persistence is present.

The only network operation in the recovered script is ping 8.8.8.8. The http://gH byte hit is a fragment of GCC runtime bug-report text built from immediates, with H supplied by the following instruction prefix. The observation is retained under a name explicitly describing URL-shaped text.

Triage behavioral process arguments independently agree with these commands. Its score-8 hidden-file finding is real. Geolocation reads accompany date formatting, and many additional spyware/adware indicators belong to the separately launched Outlook process.
samples.missing_context: Deployment and authorization for making mail backups are unknown. Hidden staging under a reserved NUL path and CertUtil execution warrant investigation, but the fully recovered payload performs the advertised local backup. Benign here is not a claim of trusted deployment.
samples.marker_line: Outlook backup wrapper: local PST/OST copy; retain hiding/decode

samples.identification: Daidriski / Joha Digital-named unsigned native x64 loader; family unconfirmed
evidence: Version claims Daidriski 5.4.3.1917 and Joha Digital GmbH are unsigned self-attestation, not verified product identity. The PE has no security-directory signature or trailing archive.

TLS initialization supplies concealed state; repeated signed relative-table dispatches flatten the code. The entry reaches 0x1400068a0. Encrypted strings and extensive filler hide API names and a second image.

Emulation recovered a complete image-layout native DLL. Reconstructing section file offsets yielded a research artifact with preferred base 0x180000000, entry RVA 0x78da0, and TLS callback 0x1800259e0. This reconstruction is not claimed to be the original distributed DLL.

The outer path resolves FindWindowA, looks up Shell_TrayWnd and obtains its PID through GetWindowThreadProcessId. With a stubbed nonzero PID, OpenProcess requests 0x1fffff. The continuation parses the selected module PE header; full injection success was not established.

The recovered DLL starts a worker (0x1800260d4). Its traced path collects firmware/memory/CPU, user locale, computer/user names, OS/volume identity, display dimensions and Uninstall registry inventories. It dynamically resolves BCrypt and WinHTTP, connects to veltrixobsidian.website:443 and issues POST /. WinHttpWriteData receives a 189-byte binary body. The host-profile upload interpretation follows this worker data path; successful remote delivery was not observed.
Concealed native staging, shell-process targeting, misleading packaging, and a configured external check-in outweigh any legitimate inventory-tool interpretation.
samples.missing_context: No operator tasking, response payload, runtime delivery success or legitimate deployment context is available. No credential theft, ransomware, mining or specific malware family is inferred.
samples.coverage_gap: Two distinct suspicious original-byte detections cover control-flow and data concealment. Custom decoding hides the DLL, endpoint and profiler APIs from the ordinary extractor; no fabricated hostile exfiltration or injection signature was added to the original-byte rules.
samples.marker_line: Daidriski loader: concealed DLL profiles host and posts to C2

evidence: The executable extracted from the official croc_v11.5.5_Windows-32bit.zip has exactly the supplied SHA-256 and length 22254080. This establishes binary integrity against the published release, despite the absent Authenticode signature.

Go build metadata identifies github.com/schollz/croc/v11, go1.27.2, GOOS=windows, GOARCH=386 and the declared dependencies. The pclntab yields main.main at 0xdd9ae0 and cli.RunContext at 0xdc34c0. Their disassembled calls match upstream signal handling, CLI dispatch and marked-file cleanup.

File transfer, PAKE/encryption, relay networking, optional explicitly selected SSH sessions, Tailscale/Tailcat transport, cloud-environment detection, and self-update support match the retrieved upstream source. There is no added wrapper, overlay or embedded attacker configuration.
The exact Tailscale dependency source explains link-local cloud metadata/token-header references as environment detection. The referenced public IP lookup is ordinary external-address discovery.

The observed Emit calls are gVisor logging, not .NET IL generation. The hujson path is a dependency reference, not Agentics identity. AdjustTokenPrivileges is a neutral capability and userspace-networking is configuration, not by itself recon or C2.

Triage static score 10 is driven by the custom INDICATOR_SUSPICIOUS_EXE_NoneWindowsUA organization rule; its behavioral task scores 3. The collector-assigned family-heavy filename is not attribution evidence.
samples.missing_context: File transfer and SSH can be abused, but no malicious invocation or deployment accompanies this identical official release.
samples.marker_line: Croc 11.5.5: byte-identical official release; correct trait scope

matcher_corrections.module_loading: The direct __import__(zlib) call and its Base64/zlib grouping were moved with exact consumers from import metadata to runtime module loading. Matchers, exclusions, effective scopes and severities remain unchanged.

consumer_audit.exact_consumers: Updated exact and same-directory references, including zlib regression assertions. The .NET preprocessor consumer retains opcode-emission coverage.
consumer_audit.ancestor_selectors: No ancestor of metadata/import/package is a YAML selector. Discovery and C2 ancestors stop treating a bare token-privilege function or userspace-networking flag as an objective; this is a correction of unsupported intent. material_detection_losses: The false .NET IL-generation claim on Croc is removed. Its ordinary logging Emit calls do not establish that behavior. No supported attack finding was lost in the three original samples or the outside-batch positive.
remaining_disagreement: The classifier still returns level -1 / class 0 for the malicious Daidriski loader: probability rose from 0.75049204 to 0.8891351. Keep this classifier miss visible; do not invent hostile traits or duplicate evidence to push the score.
archives: All three original reports contain one PE and no archive members. The two manually decoded Outlook batches (including one batch-expansion layer) were scanned separately and have no suspicious/hostile findings. The reconstructed DLL was separately inspected and scanned; it is not an engine-extracted original archive member.
